In the same way as before, this too is taught, having been brought to its conclusion and culmination for a single monk.

Kāmadhātuādīnaṃ dvedhāvitakke (ma. ni. 1.206) kāmavitakkādīsu vuttanayeneva attho veditabbo. Abhidhammepi “tattha katamā kāmadhātu, kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko”tiādinā (vibha. 182) nayeneva etāsaṃ vitthāro āgatoyeva. Imāpi cha dhātuyo heṭṭhā aṭṭhārasahiyeva pūretabbā. Pūrentena kāmadhātuto nīharitvā pūretabbā. Iti imāsu aṭṭhārasasu dhātūsu aḍḍhekādasadhātuyo rūpapariggahoti purimanayeneva idampi ekassa bhikkhuno niggamanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā kathitaṃ hoti.

Regarding 'sensuous-sphere element' and so on, the meaning should be understood by the method explained in the Dvedhāvitakka Sutta concerning thoughts of sensuality and so on. In the Abhidhamma as well, the detailed explanation of these has indeed come by the method beginning with, 'Therein, what is the sensuous-sphere element? Thought and applied thought connected with sensuality,' and so on. These six elements should also be completed by means of the eighteen below. One who is completing them should do so by extracting from the sensuous-sphere element. Thus, among these eighteen elements, ten and a half elements are the comprehension of matter. In the same way as before, this too is taught, having been brought to its conclusion and culmination for a single monk.

Kāmadhātuādīsu pañca kāmāvacarakkhandhā [P 4.0106] kāmadhātu nāma, pañca rūpāvacarakkhandhā rūpadhātu nāma, cattāro arūpāvacarakkhandhā arūpadhātu nāma. Abhidhamme pana “tattha katamā kāmadhātu, heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā”tiādinā (vibha. 182) nayena etāsaṃ vitthāro āgatoyeva. Imāpi tisso dhātuyo heṭṭhā aṭṭhārasahiyeva pūretabbā. Pūrentena kāmadhātuto nīharitvā pūretabbā. Iti imāsu aṭṭhārasasu dhātūsu aḍḍhekādasadhātuyo rūpapariggahoti purimanayeneva idampi ekassa bhikkhuno niggamanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā kathitaṃ hoti.

Regarding 'sensuous-sphere element' and so on: the five aggregates of the sensuous sphere are called the sensuous-sphere element; the five aggregates of the form sphere are called the form-sphere element; the four aggregates of the formless sphere are called the formless-sphere element. But in the Abhidhamma, the detailed explanation of these has indeed come by the method beginning with, 'Therein, what is the sensuous-sphere element? Having made the Avīci hell the lower limit,' and so on. These three elements should also be completed by means of the eighteen below. One who is completing them should do so by extracting from the sensuous-sphere element. Thus, among these eighteen elements, ten and a half elements are the comprehension of matter. In the same way as before, this too is taught, having been brought to its conclusion and culmination for a single monk.

Saṅkhatāti paccayehi samāgantvā katā, pañcannaṃ khandhānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Na saṅkhatā asaṅkhatā. Nibbānassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Imāpi dve dhātuyo heṭṭhā aṭṭhārasahiyeva pūretabbā. Pūrentena saṅkhatadhātuto nīharitvā pūretabbā. Iti imāsu aṭṭhārasasu dhātūsu aḍḍhekādasadhātuyo rūpapariggahoti purimanayeneva idampi ekassa bhikkhuno niggamanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā kathitaṃ hoti.

'Conditioned' means made by conditions having come together; this is a designation for the five aggregates. 'Unconditioned' means not conditioned; this is a designation for Nibbāna. These two elements should also be completed by means of the eighteen below. One who is completing them should do so by extracting from the conditioned element. Thus, among these eighteen elements, ten and a half elements are the comprehension of matter. In the same way as before, this too is taught, having been brought to its conclusion and culmination for a single monk.

126. Ajjhattikabāhirānīti ajjhattikāni ca bāhirāni ca. Ettha hi cakkhuādīni ajjhattikāni cha, rūpādīni bāhirāni cha. Idhāpi jānāti passatīti saha vipassanāya maggo kathito.

126. 'Internal and external' means both internal and external. For here, the six beginning with the eye are internal, and the six beginning with forms are external. Here too, by 'he knows, he sees,' the path together with insight is taught.

Imasmiṃ [V 4.0076] sati idantiādi mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaye vitthāritameva.

The phrase beginning with 'When this exists, that is,' has already been explained in detail in the Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta.

127. Aṭṭhānanti [M 4.0074] hetupaṭikkhepo. Anavakāsoti paccayapaṭikkhepo. Ubhayenāpi kāraṇameva paṭikkhipati. Kāraṇañhi tadāyattavuttitāya attano phalassa ṭhānanti ca avakāsoti ca vuccati. Yanti yena kāraṇena. Diṭṭhisampannoti [P 4.0107] maggadiṭṭhiyā sampanno sotāpanno ariyasāvako. Kañci saṅkhāranti catubhūmakesu saṅkhatasaṅkhāresu kañci ekasaṅkhārampi. Niccato upagaccheyyāti niccoti gaṇheyya. Netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti etaṃ kāraṇaṃ natthi na upalabbhati. Yaṃ puthujjanoti yena kāraṇena puthujjano. Ṭhānametaṃ vijjatīti etaṃ kāraṇaṃ atthi. Sassatadiṭṭhiyā hi so tebhūmakesu saṅkhatasaṅkhāresu kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato gaṇheyyāti attho. Catutthabhūmakasaṅkhārā pana tejussadattā divasaṃ santatto ayoguḷo viya makkhikānaṃ diṭṭhiyā vā aññesaṃ vā akusalānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ na honti. Iminā nayena kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhatotiādīsupi attho veditabbo.

127. The term 'impossible' (aṭṭhānaṃ) is a rejection of the cause. The term 'no opportunity' (anavakāso) is a rejection of the condition. By both, the Blessed One rejects the very cause. For a cause, because its effect is dependent upon it, is called the 'ground' and the 'opportunity' for its own fruit. 'That' (yaṃ) means 'by which cause.' 'One accomplished in view' (diṭṭhisampanno) is a noble disciple, a stream-enterer, accomplished in the wisdom of the path. 'Any formation' (kañci saṅkhāraṃ) means any single formation among the conditioned formations in the four planes. 'Would regard as permanent' (niccato upagaccheyya) means 'would grasp as permanent.' 'This is impossible' (netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati) means this cause does not exist, it is not found. 'That an ordinary person...' (yaṃ puthujjano) means 'by which cause an ordinary person...' 'This is possible' (ṭhānametaṃ vijjati) means this cause exists. The meaning is: indeed, due to the view of eternalism, that ordinary person would grasp some formation among the conditioned formations in the three planes as permanent. The formations of the fourth plane, however, due to their intensity—just as a red-hot iron ball during the day is not an object for flies—do not become an object for the view or for other unwholesome states. In this way, the meaning should also be understood in the sections beginning with 'any formation as pleasant.'

Sukhato upagaccheyyāti “ekantasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā”ti (ma. ni. 3.21, 22) evaṃ attadiṭṭhivasena sukhato gāhaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhivippayuttacittena pana ariyasāvako pariḷāhābhibhūto pariḷāhavūpasamatthaṃ mattahatthiṃ parittāsito viya, cokkhabrāhmaṇo viya ca gūthaṃ kañci saṅkhāraṃ sukhato upagacchati. Attavāre kasiṇādipaṇṇattisaṅgahatthaṃ saṅkhāranti avatvā kañci dhammanti vuttaṃ. Idhāpi ariyasāvakassa catubhūmakavasena veditabbo, puthujjanassa tebhūmakavasena. Sabbavāresu ariyasāvakassāpi tebhūmakavaseneva paricchedo vaṭṭati. Yaṃ yañhi puthujjano [P 4.0108] gaṇhāti, tato tato ariyasāvako gāhaṃ viniveṭheti. Puthujjano hi yaṃ yaṃ niccaṃ sukhaṃ attāti gaṇhāti, taṃ taṃ ariyasāvako aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattāti gaṇhanto taṃ gāhaṃ viniveṭheti.

'Would regard as pleasant' (sukhato upagaccheyya) is said in reference to grasping as pleasant by means of the view of self, as in 'the self is exclusively happy and free from disease after death.' But a noble disciple, with a mind disassociated from view, being overwhelmed by the fever of defilements and for the sake of quenching that fever, approaches some formation as pleasant—like one who has a protective charm approaches a maddened elephant, and like a brahmin who desires purity approaches excrement. In the section on self, in order to include concepts such as kasiṇas, instead of saying 'formation,' the Blessed One said 'any phenomenon.' Here too, this should be understood in terms of the four planes for a noble disciple, and in terms of the three planes for an ordinary person. In all sections, for the noble disciple too, the delimitation applies only in terms of the three planes. For from whatever an ordinary person grasps, from that the noble disciple disentangles the grasping. Indeed, whatever an ordinary person grasps as permanent, pleasant, and self, the noble disciple—grasping that very thing as impermanent, suffering, and non-self—disentangles that grasping.

128. Mātarantiādīsu janikāva mātā, janako pitā, manussabhūtova khīṇāsavo arahāti adhippeto. Kiṃ pana ariyasāvako aññaṃ jīvitā voropeyyāti? Etampi aṭṭhānaṃ. Sacepi hi bhavantaragataṃ ariyasāvakaṃ [M 4.0075] attano ariyabhāvaṃ ajānantampi koci evaṃ vadeyya “imaṃ kunthakipillikaṃ jīvitā voropetvā sakalacakkavāḷagabbhe cakkavattirajjaṃ paṭipajjāhī”ti[V 4.0077], neva so taṃ jīvitā voropeyya. Athāpi naṃ evaṃ vadeyya “sace imaṃ na ghātessasi, sīsaṃ te chindissāmā”ti. Sīsamevassa chindeyya, na ca so taṃ ghāteyya. Puthujjanabhāvassa pana mahāsāvajjabhāvadassanatthaṃ ariyasāvakassa ca baladīpanatthametaṃ vuttaṃ. Ayañhettha adhippāyo – sāvajjo puthujjanabhāvo, yatra hi nāma puthujjano mātughātādīnipi ānantariyāni karissati. Mahābalo ca ariyasāvako, yo etāni kammāni na karotīti.

128. In such phrases as ‘mother,’ the birth-mother is intended as ‘mother’; the birth-father is intended as ‘father’; and only a human being who is a taint-destroyed one is intended as ‘arahant.’ But would a noble disciple deprive another being of life? This too is impossible. For even if someone were to say to a noble disciple who has gone to another existence and is unaware of his own noble state, ‘Having deprived this tiny ant of life, attain universal sovereignty in the entire world-system,’ he would never deprive it of life. And if they were to say to him, ‘If you do not kill this, we will cut off your head,’ he would let his own head be cut off, but he would not kill it. This is said to show the great blameworthiness of the state of an ordinary person and to show the strength of the noble disciple. Herein, this is the intention: the state of an ordinary person is blameworthy, for an ordinary person would commit even heinous crimes with immediate result such as matricide. And the noble disciple is of great strength, for he does not commit these deeds.

Duṭṭhacittoti vadhakacittena paduṭṭhacitto. Lohitaṃ uppādeyyāti jīvamānakasarīre khuddakamakkhikāya pivanamattampi lohitaṃ uppādeyya. Saṅghaṃ bhindeyyāti samānasaṃvāsakaṃ samānasīmāya ṭhitaṃ pañcahi kāraṇehi saṅghaṃ bhindeyya. Vuttañhetaṃ “pañcahupāli ākārehi saṅgho bhijjati. Kammena uddesena voharanto anussāvanena salākaggāhenā”ti (pari. 458).

‘With a mind of ill will’ (duṭṭhacitto) means having a mind corrupted by a murderous mind. ‘To cause blood to arise’ (lohitaṃ uppādeyya) means to cause blood to arise on a living body, even as much as a small fly could drink. ‘To split the Saṅgha’ (saṅghaṃ bhindeyya) means to split a Saṅgha of those dwelling in communion, established within the same boundary, by five causes. This was said by the Blessed One: ‘Upāli, by five means the Saṅgha is split: by an act, by a recitation, by declaring, by an announcement, and by the taking of voting-tickets.’

Tattha [P 4.0109] kammenāti apalokanādīsu catūsu kammesu aññatarena kammena. Uddesenāti pañcasu pātimokkhuddesesu aññatarena uddesena. Voharantoti kathayanto, tāhi tāhi uppattīhi adhammaṃ dhammotiādīni aṭṭhārasa bhedakaravatthūni dīpento. Anussāvanenāti nanu tumhe jānātha mayhaṃ uccākulā pabbajitabhāvaṃ bahussutabhāvañca, mādiso nāma uddhammaṃ ubbinayaṃ satthusāsanaṃ gāheyyāti cittampi uppādetuṃ tumhākaṃ yuttaṃ, kiṃ mayhaṃ avīci nīluppalavanaṃ viya sītalo, kiṃ ahaṃ apāyato na bhāyāmītiādinā nayena kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvā anussāvanena. Salākaggāhenāti evaṃ anussāvetvā tesaṃ cittaṃ upatthambhetvā anivattidhamme katvā “gaṇhatha imaṃ salāka”nti salākaggāhena.

Therein, ‘by an act’ (kammena) means by one or another of the four acts, beginning with the act of announcement. ‘By a recitation’ (uddesena) means by one or another of the five recitations of the Pātimokkha. ‘By declaring’ (voharanto) means speaking, explaining the eighteen divisive matters, such as ‘what is not-Dhamma is Dhamma,’ by these and those reasons. ‘By an announcement’ (anussāvanena) means by making a verbal split in the ear by this method, saying: ‘Surely you know of my going forth from a high family and my great learning. Would a person like me grasp what is not-Dhamma and not-Vinaya as the Teacher's instruction? It is fitting for you to think thus. Is Avīci hell cool for me like a blue lotus grove? Do I not fear the lower realms?’ and so on. ‘By the taking of voting-tickets’ (salākaggāhena) means by the taking of voting-tickets, having announced thus, having strengthened their minds, having made them irreversible, and saying, ‘Take this voting-ticket.’

Ettha ca kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇaṃ, vohārānussāvanasalākaggāhā pana pubbabhāgā. Aṭṭhārasavatthudīpanavasena hi voharantena tattha rucijananatthaṃ anussāvetvā salākāya gāhitāyapi abhinnova hoti saṅgho. Yadā pana evaṃ cattāro vā atirekā vā salākaṃ gāhetvā āveṇikaṃ [M 4.0076] kammaṃ vā uddesaṃ vā karonti, tadā saṅgho bhinno nāma hoti. Evaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo saṅghaṃ bhindeyyāti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Ettāvatā mātughātādīni pañca ānantariyakammāni dassitāni honti, yāni puthujjano karoti, na ariyasāvako, tesaṃ āvibhāvatthaṃ –

And here, the act itself or the recitation is the standard, while the declaration, announcement, and taking of voting-tickets are preliminary parts. For even when one who is declaring by way of explaining the eighteen grounds has made an announcement to generate interest and the voting-tickets have been taken, the Saṅgha is still undivided. But when four or more, having had the voting-tickets taken, perform a separate act or recitation, then the Saṅgha is said to be divided. That a person accomplished in view would split the Saṅgha—this is impossible. By this much, the five heinous crimes with immediate result, such as matricide, have been shown—which an ordinary person commits, but a noble disciple does not—in order to make them manifest:

Kammato [V 4.0078] dvārato ceva, kappaṭṭhitiyato tathā;

Pākasādhāraṇādīhi, viññātabbo vinicchayo.

The determination should be understood by way of kamma and by way of door, likewise by way of lasting for the aeon, and by way of the commonality of result and so forth.

Tattha kammato tāva – ettha hi manussabhūtasseva manussabhūtaṃ mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā api parivattaliṅgaṃ jīvitā voropentassa kammaṃ ānantariyaṃ hoti, tassa vipākaṃ paṭibāhissāmīti sakalacakkavāḷaṃ mahācetiyappamāṇehi [P 4.0110] kañcanathūpehi pūretvāpi sakalacakkavāḷaṃ pūretvā nisinnabhikkhusaṅghassa mahādānaṃ datvāpi buddhassa bhagavato saṅghāṭikaṇṇaṃ amuñcanto vicaritvāpi kāyassa bhedā nirayameva upapajjati. Yo pana sayaṃ manussabhūto tiracchānabhūtaṃ mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā, sayaṃ vā tiracchānabhūto manussabhūtaṃ, tiracchānoyeva vā tiracchānabhūtaṃ jīvitā voropeti, tassa kammaṃ ānantariyaṃ na hoti, bhāriyaṃ pana hoti, ānantariyaṃ āhacceva tiṭṭhati. Manussajātikānaṃ pana vasena ayaṃ pañho kathito.

Therein, firstly by way of kamma: here, for a human being who deprives a human mother or father—even one who has changed gender—of life, the kamma is of immediate result. Thinking, ‘I will ward off its result,’ even if one were to fill the entire universe with golden stūpas the size of a great cetiya, or fill the entire universe and give a great offering to the Saṅgha of monks seated there, or wander about without letting go of the corner of the Blessed One, the Buddha’s, outer robe, with the breakup of the body, one is reborn only in hell. But as for one who, being human, deprives an animal mother or father of life, or who, being an animal, deprives a human mother or father of life, or who, being an animal, deprives an animal mother or father of life, for such a one the kamma is not of immediate result. It is, however, weighty; it stands bordering on an act of immediate result. This question, however, is discussed with reference to those of human birth.

Tattha eḷakacatukkaṃ saṅgāmacatukkaṃ coracatukkañca kathetabbaṃ. Eḷakaṃ māremīti abhisandhināpi hi eḷakaṭṭhāne ṭhitaṃ manusso manussabhūtaṃ mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā mārento ānantariyaṃ phusati. Eḷakābhisandhinā pana mātāpitāabhisandhinā vā eḷakaṃ mārento ānantariyaṃ na phusati. Mātāpitāabhisandhinā mātāpitaro mārento phusateva. Eseva nayo itarasmimpi catukkadvaye. Yathā ca mātāpitūsu, evaṃ arahantepi etāni catukkāni veditabbāni.

Therein, the tetrad of the goat, the tetrad of battle, and the tetrad of the thief should be explained. For even with the intention, ‘I will kill a goat,’ a person who kills a human mother or father who is standing in the place of a goat incurs an act of immediate result. However, one who kills a goat with the intention to kill a goat, or with the intention to kill a parent, does not incur an act of immediate result. One who kills parents with the intention to kill parents certainly incurs it. This same method applies in the other two tetrads. And as with parents, so too should these tetrads be understood regarding an Arahant.

Manussaarahantameva māretvā ānantariyaṃ phusati, na yakkhabhūtaṃ. Kammaṃ pana bhāriyaṃ, ānantariyasadisameva. Manussaarahantassa ca puthujjanakāleyeva satthappahāre vā vise vā dinnepi yadi so arahattaṃ patvā teneva marati, arahantaghāto hotiyeva. Yaṃ pana puthujjanakāle dinnaṃ dānaṃ arahattaṃ patvā paribhuñjati, puthujjanasseva dinnaṃ hoti. Sesaariyapuggale [M 4.0077] mārentassa ānantariyaṃ natthi. Kammaṃ pana bhāriyaṃ, ānantariyasadisameva.

One incurs an act of immediate result by killing only a human Arahant, not a yakkha one. The kamma, however, is weighty, just like an act of immediate result. And in the case of a human Arahant, even if a blow with a weapon or poison was given while he was still an ordinary person, if, having attained Arahantship, he dies from that very cause, it is indeed the killing of an Arahant. But a gift given while one is an ordinary person, which one partakes of after attaining Arahantship, is considered given to an ordinary person. For one who kills other noble persons, there is no act of immediate result. The kamma, however, is weighty, just like an act of immediate result.

Lohituppāde tathāgatassa abhejjakāyatāya parūpakkamena cammacchedaṃ katvā lohitapaggharaṇaṃ nāma natthi. Sarīrassa pana antoyeva ekasmiṃyeva ṭhāne lohitaṃ samosarati. Devadattena paviddhasilato [V 4.0079] bhijjitvā gatā sakalikāpi [P 4.0111] tathāgatassa pādantaṃ pahari, pharasunā pahaṭo viya pādo antolohitoyeva ahosi. Tathā karontassa ānantariyaṃ hoti. Jīvako pana tathāgatassa ruciyā satthakena cammaṃ chinditvā tamhā ṭhānā duṭṭhalohitaṃ nīharitvā phāsumakāsi, tathā karontassa puññakammameva hoti.

Regarding the causing of blood to flow: due to the Tathāgata's unbreakable body, there is no such thing as causing blood to flow by cutting the skin through another's effort. Rather, within the body itself, blood collects in one place. A splinter that broke off from a great stone slab hurled by Devadatta struck the tip of the Tathāgata's foot. The foot, as if struck by an axe, only had blood collected within. For one who does so, an act with immediate result occurs. Jīvaka, however, according to the Tathāgata's wish, cut the skin with a small knife, drew out the bad blood from that place, and brought about comfort. For one who does so, it is only a meritorious act.

Atha ye ca parinibbute tathāgate cetiyaṃ bhindanti, bodhiṃ chindanti dhātumhi upakkamanti, tesaṃ kiṃ hotīti? Bhāriyaṃ kammaṃ hoti ānantariyasadisaṃ. Sadhātukaṃ pana thūpaṃ vā paṭimaṃ vā bādhamānaṃ bodhisākhaṃ chindituṃ vaṭṭati. Sacepi tattha nilīnā sakuṇā cetiye vaccaṃ pātenti, chindituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Paribhogacetiyato hi sarīracetiyaṃ mahantataraṃ. Cetiyavatthuṃ bhinditvā gacchantaṃ bodhimūlampi chinditvā harituṃ vaṭṭati. Yā pana bodhisākhā bodhigharaṃ bādhati, taṃ geharakkhaṇatthaṃ chindituṃ na labhati, bodhiatthañhi gehaṃ, na gehatthāya bodhi. Āsanagharepi eseva nayo. Yasmiṃ pana āsanaghare dhātu nihitā hoti, tassa rakkhaṇatthāya bodhisākhaṃ chindituṃ vaṭṭati. Bodhijagganatthaṃ ojoharaṇasākhaṃ vā pūtiṭṭhānaṃ vā chindituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva, bhagavato sarīrapaṭijaggane viya puññampi hoti.

Then, what is the result for those who, after the Tathāgata has attained Parinibbāna, destroy a cetiya, cut down a Bodhi tree, or make an attempt on a relic? The kamma is heavy; it is similar to an act with immediate result. However, it is permissible to cut a Bodhi branch that is damaging a stūpa containing relics or an image. Even if birds nesting there drop excrement on the cetiya, it is indeed permissible to cut it. For a bodily cetiya is much greater than a cetiya of use. It is permissible to cut and remove even a Bodhi root that is going along breaking the cetiya ground. But a Bodhi branch that damages a Bodhi-house, one is not permitted to cut it for the sake of protecting the house, for the house is for the sake of the Bodhi, not the Bodhi for the sake of the house. In a residence hall, too, this is the same principle. But in a residence hall where a relic is enshrined, it is permissible to cut a Bodhi branch for its protection. For the maintenance of the Bodhi tree, it is indeed permissible to cut a sap-drawing branch or a rotten part; just as in tending to the Blessed One's physical body, there is also merit.

Saṅghabhede sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghe asannipatite visuṃ parisaṃ gahetvā katavohārānussāvana-salākaggāhassa kammaṃ vā karontassa, uddesaṃ vā uddisantassa bhedo ca hoti ānantariyakammañca. Samaggasaññāya pana vaṭṭatīti kammaṃ karontassa bhedova hoti, na ānantariyakammaṃ, tathā navato ūnaparisāyaṃ. Sabbantimena paricchedena [P 4.0112] navannaṃ janānaṃ yo saṅghaṃ bhindati[M 4.0078], tassa ānantariyakammaṃ hoti. Anuvattakānaṃ adhammavādīnaṃ mahāsāvajjakammaṃ. Dhammavādino pana anavajjā.

Regarding schism in the Saṅgha: when the Saṅgha within the boundary has not assembled, for one who takes a separate assembly and performs an act—such as the announcement of a formal procedure or the taking of voting tickets—or for one who recites the Pātimokkha, there is both a schism and an act with immediate result. However, for one who performs an act with the perception of unity, there is only a schism, not an act with immediate result; likewise for an assembly of less than nine. By the minimum definition, whoever among nine persons splits the Saṅgha incurs an act with immediate result. For the followers who are speakers of non-Dhamma, the act is of great fault. But for the speaker of Dhamma, there is no fault.

Tattha navannameva saṅghabhede idaṃ suttaṃ – “ekato upāli cattāro honti, ekato cattāro, navamo anussāveti, salākaṃ gāheti ‘ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, idaṃ gaṇhatha, imaṃ rocethā’ti, evaṃ kho, upāli, saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo ca. Navannaṃ vā, upāli, atirekanavannaṃ vā saṅgharāji ceva hoti saṅghabhedo cā”ti (cūḷava. 351). Etesu pana pañcasu [V 4.0080] saṅghabhedo vacīkammaṃ, sesāni kāyakammānīti. Evaṃ kammato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Therein, regarding a schism among nine, this is the Sutta: 'Upāli, on one side there are four, and on one side there are four; the ninth makes the announcement and has the voting tickets taken, saying: “This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher's instruction. Accept this, approve of this.” Thus, Upāli, there is both a crack in the Saṅgha and a schism of the Saṅgha. Upāli, with nine or with more than nine, there is both a crack in the Saṅgha and a schism of the Saṅgha.' Among these five, schism of the Saṅgha is a verbal act; the remaining are bodily acts. Thus, the determination should be known by way of the act.

Dvāratoti sabbāneva cetāni kāyadvāratopi vacīdvāratopi samuṭṭhahanti. Purimāni panettha cattāri āṇattikavijjāmayapayogavasena vacīdvārato samuṭṭhahitvāpi kāyadvārameva pūrenti, saṅghabhedo hatthamuddāya bhedaṃ karontassa kāyadvārato samuṭṭhahitvāpi vacīdvārameva pūretīti. Evamettha dvāratopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding the doors: all these acts arise from both the body-door and the speech-door. Herein, the first four, by way of application through command or through knowledge, although arising from the speech-door, fulfill only the body-door. Schism of the Saṅgha, for one who creates a split by a hand gesture, although arising from the body-door, fulfills only the speech-door. Thus, herein, the determination should be known also by way of the doors.

Kappaṭṭhitiyatoti saṅghabhedoyeva cettha kappaṭṭhitiyo. Saṇṭhahante hi kappe kappavemajjhe vā saṅghabhedaṃ katvā kappavināseyeva muccati. Sacepi hi sveva kappo vinassissatīti ajja saṅghabhedaṃ karoti, sveva muccati, ekadivasameva niraye paccati. Evaṃ karaṇaṃ pana natthi. Sesāni cattāri kammāni ānantariyāneva honti, na kappaṭṭhitiyānīti evamettha kappaṭṭhitiyatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding duration for an aeon: only schism of the Saṅgha endures for an aeon. For if one creates a schism in the Saṅgha while the aeon is established or in the middle of the aeon, one is released only at the destruction of the aeon. Even if one creates a schism today, thinking, 'The aeon will be destroyed tomorrow,' one is released tomorrow, being cooked in hell for only one day. However, such an act does not exist. The remaining four acts are only of immediate result; they do not endure for an aeon. Thus, herein, the determination should be known also by way of duration for an aeon.

Pākatoti [P 4.0113] yena ca pañcape’tāni kammāni katāni honti, tassa saṅghabhedoyeva paṭisandhivasena vipaccati, sesāni “ahosikammaṃ, nāhosi kammavipāko”ti evamādīsu saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti. Saṅghassa bhedābhāve lohituppādo, tadabhāve arahantaghāto, tadabhāve ca sace pitā sīlavā hoti, mātā dussīlā, no vā tathā sīlavatī, pitughāto paṭisandhivasena vipaccati. Sace mātāpitughāto, dvīsupi sīlena vā dussīlena vā samānesu mātughātova paṭisandhivasena vipaccati[M 4.0079]. Mātā hi dukkarakārinī bahūpakārā ca puttānanti evamettha pākatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding the ripening: for one by whom these five acts have been done, only schism of the Saṅgha ripens by way of rebirth-linking. The remaining acts are reckoned among those of which it is said, 'It was an act, but there was no result of the act.' In the absence of a schism of the Saṅgha, the drawing of blood from a Buddha ripens. In its absence, the killing of an Arahant ripens. In its absence, if the father is virtuous and the mother is unvirtuous or not similarly virtuous, the killing of the father ripens by way of rebirth-linking. If both parents are killed, and both are equal in virtue or lack of virtue, the killing of the mother ripens by way of rebirth-linking. For the mother is one who does what is difficult to do and is of great help to her children. Thus, herein, the determination should be known also by way of the ripening.

Sādhāraṇādīhīti purimāni cattāri sabbesampi gahaṭṭhapabbajitānaṃ sādhāraṇāni. Saṅghabhedo pana “na kho, upāli bhikkhunī, saṅghaṃ bhindati, na sikkhamānā, na sāmaṇero, na sāmaṇerī, na upāsako, na upāsikā saṅghaṃ bhindati, bhikkhu kho, upāli, pakatatto samānasaṃvāsako samānasīmāyaṃ ṭhito saṅghaṃ bhindatī”ti (cūḷava. 351) vacanato vuttappakārassa bhikkhunova hoti, na aññassa, tasmā asādhāraṇo. Ādisaddena sabbepi te dukkhavedanāsahagatā [V 4.0081] dosamohasampayuttā cāti evamettha sādhāraṇādīhipi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding what is common, etc.: the first four acts are common to all, householders and monastics. But schism of the Saṅgha, according to the statement, 'No, Upāli, a bhikkhunī does not split the Saṅgha, nor a female probationer, nor a male novice, nor a female novice, nor a male lay follower, nor a female lay follower. It is a bhikkhu, Upāli, a regular monk in communion and standing within the same boundary, who splits the Saṅgha,' occurs only for a bhikkhu of the type described, not for another. Therefore, it is not common. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), it is understood that all of them are accompanied by painful feeling and are conjoined with aversion and delusion. Thus, herein, the determination should be known by way of what is common, etc.

Aññaṃ satthāranti “ayaṃ me satthā satthukiccaṃ kātuṃ asamattho”ti bhavantarepi aññaṃ titthakaraṃ “ayaṃ me satthā”ti evaṃ gaṇheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti attho.

Regarding 'another teacher': The meaning is that there is no possibility that an Ariya person, even in another existence, would take another sect-founder, thinking, 'This teacher of mine is incapable of performing the duties of a teacher; this one is my teacher.'

129. Ekissā lokadhātuyāti dasasahassilokadhātuyā. Tīṇi [P 4.0114] hi khettāni jātikhettaṃ āṇākhettaṃ visayakhettaṃ. Tattha jātikhettaṃ nāma dasasahassī lokadhātu. Sā hi tathāgatassa mātukucchiokkamanakāle nikkhamanakāle sambodhikāle dhammacakkappavattane āyusaṅkhārossajjane parinibbāne ca kampati. Koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷaṃ pana āṇākhettaṃ nāma. Āṭānāṭiyamoraparittadhajaggaparittaratanaparittādīnañhi ettha āṇā vattati. Visayakhettassa pana parimāṇaṃ natthi. Buddhānañhi “yāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ tāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ, yāvatakaṃ neyyaṃ tāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ, ñāṇapariyantikaṃ neyyaṃ neyyapariyantikaṃ ñāṇa”nti (paṭi. ma. 3.5) vacanato avisayo nāma natthi.

129. 'In one world-system' means in a ten-thousand world-system. For there are three fields: the birth-field, the authority-field, and the range-field. Among these, the birth-field is the ten-thousand world-system. For it trembles at the time of the Tathāgata's descent into his mother’s womb, at his birth, at his enlightenment, at the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma, at his relinquishing of the life-force, and at his final passing away. The authority-field, on the other hand, is a hundred thousand koṭi of world-systems. For the authority of protective chants such as the Āṭānāṭiya, Mora, Dhajagga, and Ratana operates within this field. The range-field, however, has no limit. For, as it is said in the Paṭisambhidāmagga: 'As far as knowledge extends, so far extends what is to be known; as far as what is to be known extends, so far extends knowledge. The knowable is bounded by knowledge, and knowledge is bounded by the knowable.' Therefore, for the Buddhas, there is nothing that is not their object-domain.

Imesu pana tīsu khettesu ṭhapetvā imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ aññasmiṃ cakkavāḷe buddhā uppajjantīti suttaṃ natthi, na uppajjantīti pana atthi. Tīṇi piṭakāni vinayapiṭakaṃ suttantapiṭakaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ, tisso saṅgītiyo mahākassapattherassa saṅgīti, yasattherassa saṅgīti, moggaliputtatissattherassa saṅgītīti. Imā tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhe tepiṭake buddhavacane imaṃ [M 4.0080] cakkavāḷaṃ muñcitvā aññattha buddhā uppajjantīti suttaṃ natthi, na uppajjantīti pana atthi.

Furthermore, among these three fields, setting aside this world-system, there is no text stating that Buddhas arise in another world-system, but there is a text stating that they do not arise. There are three Piṭakas: the Vinaya Piṭaka, the Suttanta Piṭaka, and the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. There are three Councils: the Council of the Elder Mahākassapa, the Council of the Elder Yasa, and the Council of the Elder Moggaliputtatissa. In the word of the Buddha, the Tepiṭaka, which was established at these three Councils, there is no text stating that Buddhas arise elsewhere, setting aside this world-system; but there is a text stating that they do not arise.

Apubbaṃ acarimanti apure apacchā. Ekato na uppajjanti, pure vā pacchā vā uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha hi bodhipallaṅke bodhiṃ appatvā na uṭṭhahissāmīti nisinnakālato [P 4.0115] paṭṭhāya yāva mātukucchismiṃ paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ, tāva pubbeti na veditabbaṃ. Bodhisattassa hi paṭisandhiggahaṇena dasasahassacakkavāḷakampaneneva khettapariggaho kato, aññassa buddhassa uppatti nivāritāva hoti. Parinibbānakālato paṭṭhāya yāva sāsapamattā dhātu [V 4.0082] tiṭṭhati, tāva pacchāti na veditabbaṃ. Dhātūsu hi ṭhitāsu buddhā ṭhitāva honti. Tasmā etthantare aññassa buddhassa uppatti nivāritāva hoti. Dhātuparinibbāne pana jāte aññassa buddhassa uppatti na nivāritā.

'Not before, not after' means neither prior nor subsequent. They do not arise simultaneously; it is said that they arise either before or after. In this regard, the period from the time of sitting at the Bodhi-seat with the resolve, 'I will not rise until I attain enlightenment,' back to the taking of conception in the mother's womb, is not to be known as 'before.' For by the Bodhisatta's taking of conception, the acquisition of his field is made through the trembling of the ten-thousandfold world-system, and the arising of another Buddha is thereby prevented. From the time of the final passing away until a relic the size of a mustard seed remains, that period is not to be known as 'after.' For as long as the relics endure, the Buddhas are indeed considered to endure. Therefore, during this interval, the arising of another Buddha is indeed prevented. But when the final passing away of the relics occurs, the arising of another Buddha is not prevented.

Tīṇi hi antaradhānāni nāma pariyattiantaradhānaṃ, paṭivedhaantaradhānaṃ, paṭipattiantaradhānanti. Tattha pariyattīti tīṇi piṭakāni. Paṭivedhoti saccapaṭivedho. Paṭipattīti paṭipadā. Tattha paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi. Ekasmiñhi kāle paṭivedhadharā bhikkhū bahū honti, eso bhikkhu puthujjanoti aṅguliṃ pasāretvā dassetabbo hoti. Imasmiṃyeva dīpe ekavāre puthujjanabhikkhu nāma nāhosi. Paṭipattipūrikāpi kadāci bahū honti kadāci appā. Iti paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi, sāsanaṭṭhitiyā pana pariyatti pamāṇaṃ.

For there are three kinds of disappearance: the disappearance of the scriptural learning, the disappearance of the penetration, and the disappearance of the practice. Herein, 'scriptural learning' means the three Piṭakas. 'Penetration' means the penetration of the truths. 'Practice' means the path. In this regard, penetration and practice may or may not exist. For at one time, there are many monks who are bearers of penetration, so much so that one would have to point a finger to indicate, 'This monk is a worldling.' On this very island, there was once a time when there was no such thing as a worldling monk. Those who fulfill the practice may also at times be many, and at times be few. Thus, penetration and practice may or may not exist; but for the stability of the Dispensation, scriptural learning is the standard.

Paṇḍito hi tepiṭakaṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti. Yathā amhākaṃ bodhisatto āḷārassa santike pañcābhiññā satta ca samāpattiyo nibbattetvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā parikammaṃ pucchi, so na jānāmīti āha. Tato udakassa santikaṃ gantvā adhigataṃ visesaṃ saṃsandetvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ pucchi, so ācikkhi, tassa vacanasamanantarameva mahāsatto taṃ sampādesi, evameva paññavā bhikkhu pariyattiṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti. Tasmā [P 4.0116] pariyattiyā ṭhitāya sāsanaṃ ṭhitaṃ hoti.

For a wise person, having heard the Tepiṭaka, fulfills both practice and penetration. Just as our Bodhisatta, in the presence of Āḷāra, having developed the five higher knowledges and the seven attainments, asked about the preparatory practice for the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, and he replied, 'I do not know.' Then, going to the presence of Uddaka, and comparing the special attainment he had reached, he asked about the preparatory practice for the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Uddaka explained it, and immediately after his words, the Great Being accomplished it. In the very same way, a wise monk, having heard the scriptural learning, fulfills both. Therefore, when the scriptural learning is established, the Dispensation is established.

Yadā [M 4.0081] pana sā antaradhāyati, tadā paṭhamaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ nassati. Tattha paṭṭhānaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ antaradhāyati, anukkamena pacchā dhammasaṅgaho, tasmiṃ antarahite itaresu dvīsu piṭakesu ṭhitesu sāsanaṃ ṭhitameva hoti. Tattha suttantapiṭake antaradhāyamāne paṭhamaṃ aṅguttaranikāyo ekādasakato paṭṭhāya yāva ekakā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ saṃyuttanikāyo cakkapeyyālato paṭṭhāya yāva oghataraṇā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ majjhimanikāyo indriyabhāvanato paṭṭhāya yāva mūlapariyāyā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ dīghanikāyo dasuttarato paṭṭhāya yāva brahmajālā antaradhāyati. Ekissāpi dvinnampi gāthānaṃ pucchā addhānaṃ gacchati, sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkoti sabhiyapucchā (su. ni. sabhiyasuttaṃ) viya āḷavakapucchā (su. ni. āḷavakasuttaṃ; saṃ. ni. 1.246) [V 4.0083] viya ca. Etā kira kassapabuddhakālikā antarā sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu.

But when that scriptural learning disappears, first the Abhidhamma Piṭaka vanishes. Therein, the Paṭṭhāna vanishes first of all, and gradually thereafter the Dhammasaṅgaṇī. When that has vanished, while the other two Piṭakas remain, the Dispensation still stands. When the Suttanta Piṭaka begins to vanish, first the Aṅguttara Nikāya vanishes, starting from the Book of the Elevens down to the Book of the Ones. After that, the Saṃyutta Nikāya vanishes, from the Cakkapeyyāla section up to the Oghataraṇa Sutta. After that, the Majjhima Nikāya vanishes, from the Indriyabhāvanā Sutta down to the Mūlapariyāya Sutta. After that, the Dīgha Nikāya vanishes, from the Dasuttara Sutta down to the Brahmajāla Sutta. The questioning on even one or two verses may last for a long time, but it cannot sustain the Dispensation, like the Sabhiya's Questions and the Āḷavaka's Questions. It is said that these texts, originating from the time of Kassapa Buddha, were unable to sustain the Dispensation in the interim.

Dvīsu pana piṭakesu antarahitesupi vinayapiṭake ṭhite sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati, parivārakhandhakesu antarahitesu ubhatovibhaṅge ṭhite ṭhitameva hoti. Ubhatovibhaṅge antarahite mātikāya ṭhitāyapi ṭhitameva hoti. Mātikāya antarahitāya pātimokkhapabbajjaupasampadāsu ṭhitāsu sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati. Liṅgamaddhānaṃ gacchati, setavatthasamaṇavaṃso pana kassapabuddhakālato paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhi. Pacchimakassa pana saccapaṭivedhato pacchimakassa sīlabhedato ca paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ osakkitaṃ nāma hoti. Tato paṭṭhāya aññassa buddhassa uppatti na vāritāti.

Furthermore, even if the two Piṭakas were to disappear, the Dispensation would remain as long as the Vinaya Piṭaka remains. If the Parivāra and the Khandhakas were to disappear, it would still indeed remain as long as the Ubhatovibhaṅga remains. If the Ubhatovibhaṅga were to disappear, the Dispensation would indeed remain as long as the Mātikā remains. If the Mātikā were to disappear, the Dispensation remains as long as the Pātimokkha, the going forth, and the higher ordination remain. The outward sign endures for a long time; however, the lineage of white-robed ascetics has been unable to uphold the Dispensation since the time of the Buddha Kassapa. But from the last one's penetration of the truths and the last one's breach of virtue, the Dispensation is said to decline. From that point onward, the arising of another Buddha is not prevented.

Tīṇi parinibbānāni nāma kilesaparinibbānaṃ khandhaparinibbānaṃ dhātuparinibbānanti. Tattha kilesaparinibbānaṃ bodhipallaṅke ahosi, khandhaparinibbānaṃ kusinārāyaṃ, dhātuparinibbānaṃ anāgate bhavissati. Sāsanassa kira osakkanakāle imasmiṃ tambapaṇṇidīpe dhātuyo [P 4.0117] sannipatitvā mahācetiyaṃ gamissanti, mahācetiyato nāgadīpe rājāyatanacetiyaṃ, tato mahābodhipallaṅkaṃ gamissanti, nāgabhavanatopi devalokatopi brahmalokatopi dhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅkameva gamissanti. Sāsapamattāpi dhātu antarā na nassissati. Sabbā dhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅke rāsibhūtā suvaṇṇakkhandho viya ekagghanā hutvā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo vissajjessanti, tā dasasahassilokadhātuṃ pharissanti.

There are three kinds of Parinibbāna: the Parinibbāna of defilements, the Parinibbāna of aggregates, and the Parinibbāna of relics. Among these, the Parinibbāna of defilements occurred at the Bodhi-seat, the Parinibbāna of aggregates at Kusinārā, and the Parinibbāna of relics will take place in the future. It is said that at the time of the decline of the Dispensation, the relics in this island of Tambapaṇṇi will gather and proceed to the Mahācetiya; from the Mahācetiya, they will go to the Rājāyatana Cetiya in Nāgadīpa, and from there to the Mahābodhipallaṅka. From the Nāga realm, the deva realm, and the Brahmā realm, the relics will proceed only to the Mahābodhipallaṅka. Not even a mustard-seed-sized relic will be lost along the way. All the relics will gather at the Mahābodhipallaṅka, becoming a single mass like a great golden mound, and as a solid block, they will emit six-hued rays that will pervade the ten-thousandfold world-system.

Tato [M 4.0082] dasasahassacakkavāḷe devatā yo sannipatitvā “ajja satthā parinibbāyati, ajja sāsanaṃ osakkati, pacchimadassanaṃ dāni idaṃ amhāka”nti dasabalassa parinibbutadivasato mahantataraṃ kāruññaṃ karissanti. Ṭhapetvā anāgāmikhīṇāsave avasesā sakabhāvena saṇṭhātuṃ na sakkhissanti. Dhātūsu tejodhātu uṭṭhahitvā yāva brahmalokā uggacchissati, sāsapamattāyapi dhātuyā sati ekajālāva bhavissati, dhātūsu pariyādānaṃ gatāsu pacchijjissati. Evaṃ mahantaṃ ānubhāvaṃ dassetvā dhātūsu antarahitāsu sāsanaṃ antarahitaṃ [V 4.0084] nāma hoti. Yāva evaṃ na anantaradhāyati, tāva acarimaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyunti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

Then, the deities of the ten-thousandfold world-system will gather and lament, saying, "Today the Teacher attains Parinibbāna, today the Dispensation declines—this is now our final sight!" They will express much greater compassion than on the day the Ten-Powered One attained Parinibbāna. Except for the non-returners and arahants, the remaining deities will be unable to remain composed. From among the relics, the fire element will arise and ascend as far as the Brahmā realm. Even if only a mustard-seed-sized relic remains, it will become a single flame; when the relics are completely gone, the flame will be extinguished. After displaying such great power, when the relics have disappeared, the Dispensation is said to have disappeared. As long as it does not disappear in this way, it is considered to be 'not the final one'. Thus, the possibility that they should arise simultaneously does not exist.

Kasmā pana apubbaṃ acarimaṃ na uppajjantīti. Anacchariyattā. Buddhā hi acchariyamanussā. Yathāha – “ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso, katamo ekapuggalo, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti (a. ni. 1.171-174).

But why do they not arise simultaneously? Because it would not be wondrous. For Buddhas are wondrous persons. As it is said: "Monks, when one person arises in the world, an extraordinary person arises. Who is that one person? The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One."

Yadi ca dve vā cattāro vā aṭṭha vā soḷasa vā ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, na acchariyā bhaveyyuṃ. Ekasmiñhi vihāre dvinnaṃ cetiyānampi lābhasakkāro uḷāro na hoti bhikkhūpi bahutāya na acchariyā [P 4.0118] jātā, evaṃ buddhāpi bhaveyyuṃ. Tasmā na uppajjanti.

If two, four, eight, or sixteen were to arise together, they would not be extraordinary. For in one monastery, the gain and honor for even two cetiyas is not great, and monks, due to their great number, are not considered extraordinary; so too would Buddhas be. Therefore, they do not arise simultaneously.

Desanāya ca visesābhāvato. Yañhi satipaṭṭhānādibhedaṃ dhammaṃ eko deseti, aññena uppajjitvāpi sova desetabbo siyā. Tato na acchariyo siyā, ekasmiṃ pana dhammaṃ desente desanāpi acchariyā hoti.

Also, because there would be no distinction in the teaching. For whatever Dhamma, distinguished as the foundations of mindfulness and so on, that one Buddha teaches, another, having arisen, would have to teach that very same thing. Thus, it would not be extraordinary. But when one Buddha teaches the Dhamma, the teaching itself is extraordinary.

Vivādābhāvato ca. Bahūsu ca buddhesu uppajjantesu bahūnaṃ ācariyānaṃ antevāsikā viya “amhākaṃ buddho pāsādiko, amhākaṃ buddho madhurassaro lābhī puññavā”ti vivadeyyuṃ, tasmāpi evaṃ na uppajjanti. Apicetaṃ kāraṇaṃ milindaraññā puṭṭhena nāgasenattherena vitthāritameva. Vuttañhi (mi. pa. 5.1.1) –

And because disputes would arise. For if many Buddhas were to arise, their disciples might dispute, like the disciples of many teachers, saying, 'Our Buddha is inspiring, our Buddha has a sweet voice, our Buddha receives much gain and is meritorious.' For that reason also, they do not arise simultaneously. Moreover, this reason was explained in detail by the Venerable Nāgasena when questioned by King Milinda. For it is said:

“Tattha, bhante nāgasena, bhāsitampetaṃ bhagavatā ‘aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā [M 4.0083] apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’ti. Desentā ca, bhante nāgasena, sabbepi tathāgatā sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhamme desenti, kathayamānā ca cattāri ariyasaccāni kathenti, sikkhāpentā ca tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhāpenti, anusāsamānā ca appamādapaṭipattiyaṃ anusāsanti. Yadi, bhante nāgasena, sabbesampi tathāgatānaṃ ekā desanā ekā kathā ekā sikkhā ekā anusiṭṭhi, kena kāraṇena [V 4.0085] dve tathāgatā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti? Ekenapi tāva buddhuppādena ayaṃ loko obhāsajāto. Yadi dutiyo buddho bhaveyya, dvinnaṃ [P 4.0119] pabhāya ayaṃ loko bhiyyosomattāya obhāsajāto bhaveyya. Ovadamānā ca dve tathāgatā sukhaṃ ovadeyyuṃ, anusāsamānā ca sukhaṃ anusāseyyuṃ, tattha me kāraṇaṃ brūhi, yathāhaṃ nissaṃsayo bhaveyyanti.

"Venerable Nāgasena, it has been said by the Blessed One: ‘This is impossible, monks, it is not possible that two Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, should arise in one world-system simultaneously; such a possibility does not exist.’ Yet, Venerable Nāgasena, all the Tathāgatas teach the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, they proclaim the four Noble Truths when speaking, they train disciples in the three trainings, and they instruct in the practice of heedfulness. If, Venerable Nāgasena, all Tathāgatas have the same teaching, the same discourse, the same training, and the same instruction, then for what reason do two Tathāgatas not arise at the same moment? Even with the arising of one Buddha this world becomes illuminated. If a second Buddha were to arise, this world would be even more greatly illuminated by the radiance of the two. Two Tathāgatas advising would advise with ease, and instructing would instruct with ease. Tell me the reason for this, so that I may be free from doubt."

Ayaṃ mahārāja dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya, caleyya kampeyya nameyya onameyya vinameyya vikireyya vidhameyya viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

"Great King, this ten-thousandfold world-system can bear only one Buddha; it bears the qualities of only one Tathāgata. If a second Buddha were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world-system could not bear it; it would shake, tremble, incline, bend down, warp, scatter, be dispersed, be shattered, and be utterly destroyed; it would not remain stable."

Yathā, mahārāja, nāvā ekapurisasandhāraṇī bhaveyya. Ekasmiṃ purise abhirūḷhe sā nāvā samupādikā bhaveyya. Atha dutiyo puriso āgaccheyya tādiso āyunā vaṇṇena vayena pamāṇena kisathūlena sabbaṅgapaccaṅgena, so taṃ nāvaṃ abhirūheyya. Apinu sā mahārāja, nāvā dvinnampi dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, caleyya kampeyya nameyya onameyya vinameyya vikireyya vidhameyya viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya, osīdeyya udaketi. Evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya, caleyya…pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

Just as, great king, a boat might be capable of bearing only one person. When one person has boarded it, that boat would be evenly balanced. Then a second person were to come, similar in age, complexion, years, stature, whether thin or stout, and in all major and minor limbs, and he were to board that boat. Great king, could that boat then bear both of them?" "Indeed not, venerable sir. It would shake, tremble, incline, bend down, warp, scatter, be dispersed, be shattered, and be utterly destroyed; it would not attain stability and would sink in the water." "In the same way, great king, this ten-thousandfold world-system is capable of bearing one Buddha; it bears the qualities of only one Tathāgata. If a second Buddha were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world-system could not bear it; it would shake... it would not attain stability.

Yathā vā pana mahārāja puriso yāvadatthaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya chādentaṃ yāvakaṇṭhamabhipūrayitvā, so dhāto pīṇito paripuṇṇo nirantaro tandikato anonamitadaṇḍajāto punadeva tattakaṃ bhojanaṃ [M 4.0084] bhuñjeyya, apinu kho, mahārāja, puriso sukhito bhaveyyāti? Na hi, bhante, sakiṃ bhuttova mareyyāti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī [P 4.0120]…pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyyāti.

Or again, great king, suppose a man were to eat as much of a pleasing meal as he desired, filling himself up to the throat. That man, being satisfied, gratified, full, with no space remaining, would become stiff like a staff, like an unbending staff. If he were then to eat that same amount of food again, great king, would that man be at ease?" "Indeed not, venerable sir. Having eaten that one time more, he would die." "In the same way, great king, this ten-thousandfold world-system is capable of bearing one Buddha... it would not attain stability.

Kiṃ nu kho, bhante nāgasena, atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti? Idha, mahārāja, dve sakaṭā ratanaparipūritā bhaveyyuṃ yāva mukhasamā. Ekasmā sakaṭato ratanaṃ gahetvā ekasmiṃ sakaṭe ākireyyuṃ, apinu kho taṃ, mahārāja, sakaṭaṃ dvinnampi sakaṭānaṃ ratanaṃ dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, nābhipi tassa phaleyya, arāpi tassa bhijjeyyuṃ, nemipi tassa opateyya, akkhopi [V 4.0086] tassa bhijjeyyāti. Kiṃ nu kho, mahārāja, atiratanabhārena sakaṭaṃ bhijjatīti? Āma, bhanteti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti.

Venerable Nāgasena, does the earth shake because of the burden of the excellent Dhamma?" "Here, great king, suppose there were two carts filled with jewels up to the brim. If one were to take jewels from one cart and pour them into the other cart, great king, could that cart bear the jewels of both carts?" "Indeed not, venerable sir. Its hub would split, its spokes would break, its rim would fall off, and its axle would break." "Great king, does the cart break because of the burden of the excellent jewels?" "Yes, venerable sir." "In the same way, great king, the earth shakes because of the burden of the excellent Dhamma.

Apica mahārāja imaṃ kāraṇaṃ buddhabalaparidīpanāya osāritaṃ, aññampi tattha abhirūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya – “tumhākaṃ buddho amhākaṃ buddho”ti ubhatopakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ. Yathā, mahārāja, dvinnaṃ balavāmaccānaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘tumhākaṃ amacco amhākaṃ amacco’ti ubhatopakkhajātā honti, evameva kho, mahārāja, yadi, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘tumhākaṃ buddho amhākaṃ buddho’ti ubhatopakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ. Idaṃ tāva, mahārāja, ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Moreover, great king, this reason has been recited to reveal the power of the Buddha. Listen also to another fitting reason therein, for which reason two Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise at the same moment. If, great king, two Perfectly Enlightened Ones were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assembly—'Your Buddha, our Buddha'—and they would become two separate factions. Just as, great king, a dispute arises in the assembly of two powerful ministers—'Your minister, our minister'—and they become two separate factions, in the same way, great king, if two Perfectly Enlightened Ones were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assembly—'Your Buddha, our Buddha'—and they would become two separate factions. This, great king, is the first reason for which two Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise at the same moment.

Aparampi, mahārāja, uttariṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, aggo buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Jeṭṭho buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Seṭṭho buddhoti, visiṭṭho buddhoti, uttamo buddhoti, pavaro buddhoti, asamo buddhoti, asamasamo buddhoti, appaṭisamo buddhoti, appaṭibhāgo buddhoti, appaṭipuggalo buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ[P 4.0121], taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Idampi kho tvaṃ, mahārāja[M 4.0085], kāraṇaṃ atthato sampaṭiccha, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Furthermore, great king, listen to another, more profound reason for which two Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise at the same moment. If, great king, two Perfectly Enlightened Ones were to arise at the same moment, the statement, 'The Buddha is Foremost,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Chief,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Best,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Distinguished,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Highest,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Most Excellent,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Unequalled,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Equal to the Unequalled,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Incomparable,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is Without a Counterpart,' would be false. The statement, 'The Buddha is a Peerless Individual,' would be false. You should accept this reason also by its meaning, great king, for which two Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not arise at the same moment.

Apica kho mahārāja buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ sabhāvapakati esā, yaṃ ekoyeva buddho loke uppajjati. Kasmā kāraṇā? Mahantatāya sabbaññubuddhaguṇānaṃ. Aññampi mahārāja yaṃ loke mahantaṃ, taṃ ekaṃyeva hoti. Pathavī, mahārāja, mahantī, sā ekāyeva. Sāgaro mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sineru girirājā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Ākāso mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sakko mahanto, so ekoyeva. Māro mahanto, so ekoyeva. Brahmā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho mahanto, so ekoyeva lokasmiṃ. Yattha te uppajjanti, tattha aññassa [V 4.0087] okāso na hoti. Tasmā, mahārāja, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho ekoyeva lokasmiṃ uppajjatīti. Sukathito, bhante nāgasena, pañho opammehi kāraṇehī”ti.

Furthermore, great king, this is the inherent nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, that only one Buddha arises in the world. For what reason? Because of the greatness of the qualities of an Omniscient Buddha. Moreover, great king, whatever is great in the world is one only. The earth, great king, is great; it is one only. The ocean is great; it is one only. Sineru, the king of mountains, is great; it is one only. The sky is great; it is one only. Sakka is great; he is one only. Māra is great; he is one only. Brahmā is great; he is one only. The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is great; He is one only in the world. Where they arise, there is no opportunity for another. Therefore, great king, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One arises as one only in the world." "Well spoken, venerable Nāgasena, is the question, with similes and reasons."

Ekissā lokadhātuyāti ekasmiṃ cakkavāḷe. Heṭṭhā imināva padena dasacakkavāḷasahassāni gahitāni tānipi, ekacakkavāḷeneva paricchindituṃ vaṭṭanti. Buddhā hi uppajjamānā imasmiṃyeva cakkavāḷe uppajjanti, uppajjanaṭṭhāne pana vārite ito aññesu cakkavāḷesu nuppajjantīti vāritameva hoti.

'In a single world-system' means in one Cakkavāḷa. Herein, by this very term, ten thousand Cakkavāḷas are included. Even those, it is proper to delimit as one Cakkavāḷa. For Buddhas, when arising, arise only in this very Cakkavāḷa. However, the place of arising being restricted, it is thereby prevented that they arise in other Cakkavāḷas apart from this one; thus it is indeed prevented.

Apubbaṃ acarimanti ettha cakkaratanapātubhāvato pubbe pubbaṃ, tasseva antaradhānato pacchā carimaṃ. Tattha dvidhā cakkaratanassa antaradhānaṃ hoti, cakkavattino kālaṃkiriyato vā pabbajjāya vā. Antaradhāyamānañca pana taṃ kālaṃkiriyato vā pabbajjato vā sattame divase antaradhāyati, tato paraṃ cakkavattino pātubhāvo avārito.

In the phrase “Not before, not after” (apubbaṃ acariman), herein, 'before' (pubbaṃ) refers to the time before the appearance of the wheel-gem, and 'after' (carimaṃ) refers to the time after its disappearance. In this regard, the disappearance of the wheel-gem occurs in two ways: either due to the death of the wheel-turning monarch or due to his going forth. Furthermore, when it is disappearing, it disappears on the seventh day from his death or his going forth. After that, the appearance of another wheel-turning monarch is not prevented.

Kasmā pana ekacakkavāḷe dve cakkavattino nuppajjantīti[P 4.0122]. Vivādupacchedato acchariyabhāvato cakkaratanassa mahānubhāvato ca. Dvīsu hi uppajjantesu “amhākaṃ rājā mahanto amhākaṃ rājā mahanto”ti vivādo uppajjeyya. Ekasmiṃ dīpe cakkavattīti ca ekasmiṃ dīpe cakkavattīti ca anacchariyā bhaveyyuṃ[M 4.0086]. Yo cāyaṃ cakkaratanassa dvisahassadīpaparivāresu catūsu mahādīpesu issariyānuppadānasamattho mahānubhāvo, so parihāyetha. Iti vivādupacchedato acchariyabhāvato cakkaratanassa mahānubhāvato ca na ekacakkavāḷe dve uppajjanti.

But why do two wheel-turning monarchs not arise in one world-system? Due to the prevention of disputes, due to the absence of the wondrous, and due to the great power of the wheel-gem. For if two were to arise, a dispute would arise, with people saying, “Our king is great! Our king is great!” And “a wheel-turning monarch on one continent” and “a wheel-turning monarch on another continent” would not be wondrous. Furthermore, that great power of the wheel-gem, which is capable of producing sovereignty over the four great continents with their two thousand surrounding islands, would diminish. Thus, due to the prevention of disputes, due to the absence of the wondrous, and due to the great power of the wheel-gem, two do not arise in one world-system.

130. Yaṃ itthī assa arahaṃ sammāsambuddhoti ettha tiṭṭhatu tāva sabbaññuguṇe nibbattetvā lokuttāraṇasamattho buddhabhāvo, paṇidhānamattampi itthiyā na sampajjati.

130. Regarding the statement, “That a woman might be an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One”: let alone the state of Buddhahood, which is capable of saving the world after having brought into being the qualities of omniscience; for a woman, even the mere aspiration is not fulfilled.

Manussattaṃ liṅgasampatti, hetu satthāradassanaṃ;

Pabbajjā guṇasampatti, adhikāro ca chandatā;

Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānā, abhinīhāro samijjhatīti. (bu. vaṃ. 2.59) –

“Human existence, perfection of the [male] characteristic, the [requisite] cause, seeing the Teacher; The state of a renunciant, the attainment of special qualities, the undertaking, and intense desire; Through the combination of these eight conditions, the great aspiration is fulfilled.”

Imāni [V 4.0088] hi paṇidhānasampattikāraṇāni. Iti paṇidhānampi sampādetuṃ asamatthāya itthiyā kuto buddhabhāvoti “aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī assa arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti vuttaṃ. Sabbākāraparipūro ca puññussayo sabbākāraparipūrameva attabhāvaṃ nibbattetīti purisova arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho.

Indeed, these are the causes for the fulfillment of the aspiration. Thus, for a woman who is incapable of fulfilling even the aspiration, whence could there be the state of Buddhahood? Therefore, it was said: “This is impossible, it is not a possibility that a woman might be an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.” And since an accumulation of merit that is complete in all aspects produces an individual existence that is itself complete in all aspects, it is only a man who becomes an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattītiādīsupi yasmā itthiyā [P 4.0123] kosohitavatthaguyhatādīnaṃ abhāvena lakkhaṇāni na paripūrenti, itthiratanābhāvena sattaratanasamaṅgitā na sampajjati, sabbamanussehi ca adhiko attabhāvo na hoti, tasmā “aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ itthī rājā assa cakkavattī”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā ca sakkattādīni tīṇi ṭhānāni uttamāni, itthiliṅgañca hīnaṃ, tasmā tassā sakkattādīnipi paṭisiddhāni.

Also in such statements as, “That a woman might be a wheel-turning monarch”: because for a woman, due to the absence of having the private parts concealed in a sheath and so on, the marks of a Great Man are not fulfilled; due to the absence of the woman-gem, the state of being endowed with the seven gems is not fulfilled; and her individual existence is not superior to all humans, therefore it was said: “This is impossible, it is not a possibility that a woman might be a wheel-turning monarch.” And because the three positions, such as the state of Sakka, are supreme, and the female characteristic is inferior, therefore for her, the states of Sakka and so on are also denied.

Nanu ca yathā itthiliṅgaṃ, evaṃ purisaliṅgampi brahmaloke natthi? Tasmā “yaṃ puriso brahmattaṃ kareyya, ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”tipi na vattabbaṃ siyāti. No na vattabbaṃ. Kasmā? Idha purisassa tattha nibbattanato. Brahmattanti hi mahābrahmattaṃ adhippetaṃ. Itthī ca idha jhānaṃ bhāvetvā kālaṃ katvā brahmapārisajjānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati, na mahābrahmānaṃ, puriso pana tattha na uppajjatīti na vattabbo. Samānepi cettha ubhayaliṅgābhāve purisasaṇṭhānāva brahmāno, na itthisaṇṭhānā, tasmā suvuttamevetaṃ.

But is it not so that just as the female characteristic does not exist in the Brahma-world, so too the male characteristic does not exist? Therefore, should it not also be said, “That a man might attain the state of Brahma, this is a possibility”? No, it is not that it should not be said. Why? Because a man from here is reborn there. For by 'the state of Brahma' is meant the state of a Mahābrahmā. And a woman, having developed jhāna here and passed away, is reborn into the company of the Retinue of Brahmā, not of the Mahābrahmās. But it cannot be said that a man is not reborn there. And although the absence of both characteristics is the same in that world, the Brahmās have only a male form, not a female form. Therefore, this was well said.

131. Kāyaduccaritassātiādīsu [M 4.0087] yathā nimbabījakosātakībījādīni madhuraphalaṃ na nibbattenti, asātaṃ amadhurameva nibbattenti, evaṃ kāyaduccaritādīni madhuravipākaṃ na nibbattenti, amadhurameva vipākaṃ nibbattenti. Yathā ca ucchubījasālibījādīni madhuraṃ sādurasameva phalaṃ nibbattenti, na asātaṃ kaṭukaṃ, evaṃ [P 4.0124] kāyasucaritādīni madhurameva vipākaṃ nibbattenti, na amadhuraṃ. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

131. In the text beginning with “Of bodily misconduct...”: just as seeds of nimba, kosātakī, and so on do not produce sweet fruit, but produce only unpleasant, non-sweet fruit, so too bodily misconduct and so on do not produce a sweet result, but produce only a non-sweet result. And just as seeds of sugarcane, rice, and so on produce fruit that is sweet and of pleasant taste, not unpleasant and bitter, so too bodily good conduct and so on produce only a sweet result, not a non-sweet one. And this was also said:

“Yādisaṃ vapate bījaṃ, tādisaṃ harate phalaṃ;

Kalyāṇakārī kalyāṇaṃ, pāpakārī ca pāpaka”nti. (saṃ. ni. 1.256);

“Whatever kind of seed one sows, that kind of fruit one reaps. One who does good reaps good, and one who does evil reaps evil.”

Tasmā [V 4.0089] “aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ kāyaduccaritassā”tiādi vuttaṃ.

Therefore, the text beginning with, “This is impossible, it is not a possibility that for bodily misconduct...” was said.

Kāyaduccaritasamaṅgītiādīsu samaṅgīti pañcavidhā samaṅgitā āyūhanasamaṅgitā cetanāsamaṅgitā kammasamaṅgitā vipākasamaṅgitā, upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitāti. Tattha kusalākusalakammāyūhanakkhaṇe āyūhanasamaṅgitāti vuccati. Tathā cetanāsamaṅgitā. Yāva pana arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva sabbepi sattā pubbe upacitaṃ vipākārahaṃ kammaṃ sandhāya “kammasamaṅgino”ti vuccanti, esā kammasamaṅgitā. Vipākasamaṅgitā vipākakkhaṇeyeva veditabbā. Yāva pana sattā arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva nesaṃ tato tato cavitvā niraye tāva uppajjamānānaṃ aggijālalohakumbhiādīhi upaṭṭhānākārehi nirayo, gabbhaseyyakattaṃ āpajjamānānaṃ mātukucchi, devesu uppajjamānānaṃ kapparukkhavimānādīhi upaṭṭhānākārehi devalokoti evaṃ uppattinimittaṃ upaṭṭhāti, iti nesaṃ iminā uppattinimittaupaṭṭhānena aparimuttatā upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā nāma. Sā calati sesā niccalā. Niraye hi upaṭṭhitepi devaloko upaṭṭhāti, devaloke upaṭṭhitepi nirayo upaṭṭhāti, manussaloke upaṭṭhitepi tiracchānayoni upaṭṭhāti, tiracchānayoniyā ca upaṭṭhitāyapi manussaloko upaṭṭhātiyeva.

In the text beginning with “endowed with bodily misconduct...”: “endowed” (samaṅgī) refers to five kinds of endowment (samaṅgitā): endowment through accumulation, endowment through volition, endowment through kamma, endowment through result, and endowment through presentation. Therein, at the moment of accumulating wholesome or unwholesome kamma, it is called “endowment through accumulation.” Likewise for “endowment through volition.” Furthermore, as long as any beings have not attained Arahantship, they are all called “endowed with kamma” with reference to previously accumulated kamma that is fit to give a result; this is “endowment through kamma.” “Endowment through result” is to be understood only at the moment of the result. Furthermore, as long as beings have not attained Arahantship, for them, having passed away from one state or another, the sign of rebirth appears thus: for those being reborn in hell, hell appears with forms of presentation such as flames of fire and iron cauldrons; for those taking conception in a womb, the mother's womb appears; for those being reborn among the devas, the deva-world appears with forms of presentation such as wish-fulfilling trees and celestial mansions. Thus, their state of not being liberated from this presentation of the sign of rebirth is called “endowment through presentation.” That one is changeable; the others are unchangeable. For even when hell has appeared, the deva-world can appear; when the deva-world has appeared, hell can appear; when the human world has appeared, the animal realm can appear; and even when the animal realm has appeared, the human world can still appear.

Tatridaṃ [P 4.0125] vatthu – soṇagiripāde kira acelavihāre soṇatthero nāma eko dhammakathiko, tassa pitā sunakhajīviko ahosi. Thero taṃ paṭibāhantopi saṃvare ṭhapetuṃ asakkonto “mā nassi jarako”ti [M 4.0088] mahallakakāle akāmakaṃ pabbājesi. Tassa gilānaseyyāya nipannassa nirayo upaṭṭhāti, soṇagiripādato mahantā mahantā sunakhā āgantvā khāditukāmā viya samparivāresuṃ. So mahābhayabhīto – “vārehi, tāta soṇa, vārehi, tāta soṇā”ti āha. Kiṃ mahātherāti. Na passasi tātāti taṃ pavattiṃ ācikkhi. Soṇatthero – “kathañhi nāma mādisassa pitā niraye nibbattissati, patiṭṭhā’ssa bhavissāmī”ti sāmaṇerehi nānāpupphāni āharāpetvā cetiyaṅgaṇabodhiyaṅgaṇesu talasantharaṇapūjaṃ āsanapūjañca kāretvā pitaraṃ mañcena cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ āharitvā mañce nisīdāpetvā – “ayaṃ mahāthera-pūjā tumhākaṃ atthāya katā ‘ayaṃ me bhagavā duggatapaṇṇākāro’ti vatvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā cittaṃ pasādehī”ti āha. So mahāthero pūjaṃ disvā tathā karonto cittaṃ pasādesi, tāvadevassa devaloko upaṭṭhāsi, nandanavana-cittalatāvana-missakavana-phārusakavanavimānāni ceva nāṭakāni ca parivāretvā ṭhitāni [V 4.0090] viya ahesuṃ. So “apetha apetha soṇā”ti āha. Kimidaṃ therāti? Etā te, tāta, mātaro āgacchantīti[P 4.0126]. Thero “saggo upaṭṭhito mahātherassā”ti cintesi. Evaṃ upaṭṭhānasamaṅgitā calatīti veditabbā. Etāsu samaṅgitāsu idha āyūhanacetanākammasamaṅgitāvasena kāyaduccaritasamaṅgītiādi vuttaṃ.

Here is the story: At the foot of Soṇagiri, it is said, in the Acela monastery, there was a Dhamma preacher named Elder Soṇa. His father made a living by means of dogs. Though the elder tried to restrain him, he was unable to establish him in restraint and, thinking, "Let not the old man perish," he ordained him in his old age against his will. When his father lay on his sickbed, hell appeared to him. Very large dogs from the foot of Soṇagiri came and surrounded him as if wishing to devour him. He, terrified by great fear, cried out, "Ward them off, dear Soṇa, ward them off, dear Soṇa!" The elder asked, "What, Great Elder?" "Do you not see, dear son?" he said, and related the event. Elder Soṇa thought, "How indeed could the father of one such as I be reborn in hell? I will be a support for him." He had novices bring various flowers and had offerings of flowers spread on the ground and offerings of seats made in the courtyards of the cetiya and the Bodhi tree. Then he had his father brought on a bed to the cetiya courtyard, had him seated on the bed, and said, "Great Elder, this offering has been made for your sake. Saying, 'Blessed One, this is my gift, the gift of a poor person,' pay homage to the Blessed One and gladden your mind." The Great Elder, seeing the offering and doing so, gladdened his mind. At that very moment, the deva world appeared to him. The celestial mansions of Nandana Grove, Cittalatā Grove, Missaka Grove, and Phārusaka Grove, along with celestial dancers, seemed to be standing surrounding him. He said, "Soṇa, let them go away! Let them go away!" When asked, "What is this, Elder?" he replied, "Dear son, these mothers of yours are coming." The elder thought, "Heaven has appeared to the Great Elder." Thus, it should be known that the endowment of presentation is changeable. Among these endowments, here "endowed with bodily misconduct," etc., is stated by way of the endowment of accumulation, volition, and kamma.

132. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānandoti “evaṃ bhagavatā imasmiṃ sutte vutte thero ādito paṭṭhāya sabbasuttaṃ samannāharitvā evaṃ sassirikaṃ katvā desitasuttassa nāma bhagavatā nāmaṃ na gahitaṃ. Handassa nāmaṃ gaṇhāpessāmī”ti cintetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca.

132. Regarding 'When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda': When this sutta was thus spoken by the Blessed One, the elder, having reflected upon the entire sutta from the beginning, thought: 'The Blessed One has not given a name to this sutta that has been taught with such splendor. Let me now request that he give it a name.' Having thought thus, he said this to the Blessed One.

Tasmā tiha tvantiādīsu ayaṃ atthayojanā –

In the phrases beginning with 'Therefore, you here,' this is the application of the meaning:

Ānanda, yasmā imasmiṃ dhammapariyāye “aṭṭhārasa kho imā, ānanda, dhātuyo, cha imā, ānanda, dhātuyo”ti evaṃ bahudhātuyo vibhattā, tasmā tiha tvaṃ imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ bahudhātukotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā panettha dhātuāyatanapaṭiccasamuppādaṭṭhānāṭṭhānavasena cattāro parivaṭṭā kathitā[M 4.0089], tasmā catuparivaṭṭotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca ādāsaṃ olokentassa mukhanimittaṃ viya imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ olokentassa ete dhātuādayo atthā pākaṭā honti, tasmā dhammādāsotipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca yathā nāma parasenamaddanā yodhā saṅgāmatūriyaṃ paggahetvā parasenaṃ pavisitvā sapatte madditvā attano jayaṃ gaṇhanti, evameva kilesasenamaddanā yogino idha vuttavasena vipassanaṃ paggahetvā kilese madditvā attano arahattajayaṃ gaṇhanti, tasmā amatadundubhītipi naṃ dhārehi. Yasmā ca yathā saṅgāmayodhā [P 4.0127] pañcāvudhaṃ gahetvā parasenaṃ viddhaṃsetvā jayaṃ gaṇhanti, evaṃ yoginopi idha vuttaṃ vipassanāvudhaṃ gahetvā kilesasenaṃ viddhaṃsetvā arahattajayaṃ gaṇhanti. Tasmā anuttaro saṅgāmavijayotipi naṃ dhārehīti.

Ānanda, because in this exposition of the Dhamma, 'These, Ānanda, are the eighteen elements; these, Ānanda, are the six elements,' and so forth, many elements are analyzed, therefore, you should remember this exposition of the Dhamma also as the 'Bahudhātuka' (Many Elements). Because herein, by way of elements, sense bases, dependent origination, and the possible and impossible, four cycles are taught, therefore, you should remember it also as the 'Catuparivaṭṭa' (Four Cycles). And because, just as for a person looking into a mirror the reflection of the face becomes clear, so for a person looking into this Dhamma exposition, these meanings beginning with the elements become clear, therefore, you should remember it also as the 'Dhammādāsa' (Mirror of the Dhamma). And because, just as warriors who crush the armies of others, having taken up the battle drum, crush the enemies and seize their own victory, even so, yogis who crush the army of defilements, having taken up insight by way of what is taught herein, crush the defilements and seize their own victory of Arahantship, therefore, you should remember it also as the 'Amatadundubhi' (Drum of the Deathless). And because, just as warriors in battle, having taken the five weapons, destroy the army of others and seize victory, so too, yogis, having taken up the weapon of insight taught herein, destroy the army of defilements and seize the victory of Arahantship. Therefore, you should remember it as the 'Anuttaro Saṅgāmavijayo' (Unsurpassed Victory in Battle).

Papañcasūdaniyā majjhimanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

From the Papañcasūdanī, the Commentary on the Majjhima Nikāya.

Bahudhātukasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Bahudhātuka Sutta is finished.

6. Isigilisuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Isigili Sutta

133. Evaṃ [V 4.0091] me sutanti isigilisuttaṃ. Tattha aññāva samaññā ahosīti isigilissa isigilīti samaññāya uppannakāle vebhāro na vebhāroti paññāyittha, aññāyevassa samaññā ahosi. Aññā paññattīti idaṃ purimapadasseva vevacanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo.

133. 'Thus have I heard' refers to the Isigili Sutta. Therein, as to 'another designation existed,' it means that at the time the designation 'Isigili' arose for the Isigili mountain, the Vebhāra mountain was not known as 'Vebhāra'; another designation indeed existed for it. This phrase 'another concept' is a synonym for the preceding term. This same method should be understood in the remaining cases as well.

Tadā kira bhagavā sāyanhasamaye samāpattito vuṭṭhāya gandhakuṭito nikkhamitvā yasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinnānaṃ pañca pabbatā paññāyanti, tattha bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisīditvā ime pañca pabbate paṭipāṭiyā ācikkhi. Tattha na bhagavato pabbatehi attho atthi, iti imesu pana pabbatesu paṭipāṭiyā kathiyamānesu isigilissa isigilibhāvo kathetabbo hoti. Tasmiṃ kathiyamāne padumavatiyā puttānaṃ pañcasatānaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni ceva padumavatiyā ca patthanā kathetabbā bhavissatīti bhagavā imaṃ pañca pabbatapaṭipāṭiṃ ācikkhi.

It is said that at that time, the Blessed One, having arisen from attainment in the evening, emerged from the Perfumed Chamber and, surrounded by the community of monks, sat down in a place where, for those seated, five mountains were visible. There he pointed out these five mountains in sequence. In this, the Blessed One had no particular purpose concerning the mountains, but as these mountains were being spoken of in sequence, the fact of Isigili being Isigili had to be told. When that was being told, the names of the five hundred Paccekabuddhas who were the sons of Padumavatī, and the aspiration of Padumavatī, would have to be told. For this reason, the Blessed One pointed out this sequence of five mountains.

Pavisantā [M 4.0090] dissanti paviṭṭhā na dissantīti yathāphāsukaṭṭhāne piṇḍāya caritvā katabhattakiccā āgantvā cetiyagabbhe yamakamahādvāraṃ vivarantā viya taṃ pabbataṃ dvedhā katvā anto pavisitvā [P 4.0128] rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānāni māpetvā tattha vasiṃsu, tasmā evamāha. Ime isīti ime paccekabuddhaisī.

'Entering, they are seen; having entered, they are not seen' means that after wandering for alms in a suitable place and having completed their meal, the Paccekabuddhas would come and, as if opening the great twin doors of a shrine chamber, they would divide that mountain in two, enter inside, create places for staying at night and during the day, and dwell there. Therefore, it was said thus. 'These seers' means these Paccekabuddha seers.

Kadā pana te tattha vasiṃsu? Atīte kira anuppanne tathāgate bārāṇasiṃ upanissāya ekasmiṃ gāmake ekā kuladhītā khettaṃ rakkhamānā ekassa paccekabuddhassa pañcahi lājāsatehi saddhiṃ ekaṃ padumapupphaṃ datvā pañca puttasatāni patthesi. Tasmiṃyeva ca khaṇe pañcasatā migaluddakā madhuramaṃsaṃ datvā “etissā puttā bhaveyyāmā”ti patthayiṃsu. Sā yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā devaloke nibbattā, tato cutā jātassare padumagabbhe nibbatti. Tameko tāpaso disvā paṭijaggi, tassā vicarantiyāva pāduddhāre pāduddhāre bhūmito padumāni uṭṭhahanti. Eko vanacarako disvā bārāṇasirañño ārocesi. Rājā naṃ āharāpetvā aggamahesiṃ [V 4.0092] akāsi, tassā gabbho saṇṭhāsi. Mahāpadumakumāro mātukucchiyaṃ vasi, sesā gabbhamalaṃ nissā nibbattā. Vayappattā uyyāne padumassare kīḷantā ekekasmiṃ padume nisīditvā khayavayaṃ paṭṭhapetvā paccekabodhiñāṇaṃ nibbattayiṃsu. Ayaṃ tesaṃ byākaraṇagāthā ahosi –

But when did they dwell there? It is said that in the past, when a Tathāgata had not arisen, near Bārāṇasī in a certain small village, a clanswoman, while guarding a field, gave a single lotus flower together with five hundred fried grains to a Paccekabuddha and aspired for five hundred sons. At that very moment, five hundred deer hunters gave sweet meat and aspired, 'May we become her sons.' She, having remained for her lifespan, was reborn in a deva world. Passing away from there, she was reborn in a lotus womb in a natural lake. A certain ascetic saw her and took care of her. As she walked about, at every footstep lotuses arose from the ground. A forest-dweller saw this and informed the king of Bārāṇasī. The king had her brought and made her his chief queen. She conceived. The prince Mahāpaduma dwelt in his mother's womb; the rest were born of moisture, arising from the impurities of the womb. Having come of age, while playing in the garden's lotus pond, sitting on individual lotuses, they established contemplation on decay and passing away and brought forth the knowledge of Paccekabodhi. This was their verse of declaration:

“Saroruhaṃ padumapalāsapattajaṃ, supupphitaṃ bhamaragaṇānuciṇṇaṃ;

Aniccatāyupagataṃ viditvā, eko care khaggavisāṇakappo”ti.

Having known that the lake-born lotus, sprung from lotus petals and leaves, well-blossomed and frequented by swarms of bees, is subject to impermanence, one should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.

Tasmiṃ [P 4.0129] kāle te tattha vasiṃsu, tadā cassa pabbatassa isigilīti samaññā udapādi.

At that time they dwelt there, and it was then that the designation 'Isigili' arose for that mountain.

135. Ye sattasārāti ariṭṭho upariṭṭho tagarasikhī yasassī sudassano piyadassī gandhāro piṇḍolo upāsabho nīto tatho sutavā bhāvitattoti terasannaṃ paccekabuddhānaṃ nāmāni vatvā idāni tesañca aññesañca gāthābandhena nāmāni ācikkhanto ye sattasārātiādimāha[M 4.0091]. Tattha sattasārāti sattānaṃ sārabhūtā. Anīghāti niddukkhā. Nirāsāti nittaṇhā.

135. Regarding 'Those who are the essence of beings': Having stated the names of the thirteen Paccekabuddhas—Ariṭṭha, Upariṭṭha, Tagarasikhī, Yasassī, Sudassana, Piyadassī, Gandhāra, Piṇḍola, Upāsabha, Nīta, Tatha, Sutavā, and Bhāvitatta—now, pointing out their names and those of others by way of verse, he said what begins with 'Those who are the essence of beings.' Therein, 'essence of beings' means they are the essence of beings. 'Without affliction' means without suffering. 'Without longing' means without craving.

Dve jālinoti cūḷajāli mahājālīti dve jālināmakā. Santacittoti idampi ekassa nāmameva. Passi jahi upadhidukkhamūlanti ettha passi nāma so paccekabuddho, dukkhassa pana mūlaṃ upadhiṃ jahīti ayamassa thuti. Aparājitotipi ekassa nāmameva.

'The two Jālīs' means the two with the name Jālī: Cūḷajālī and Mahājālī. 'Santacitta' is also the name of one. In 'Passi abandoned the substrate, the root of suffering,' Passi is the name of that Paccekabuddha, but 'he abandoned the substrate, the root of suffering' is his praise. 'Aparājita' is also the name of one.
